newsitem.title: USA: Appliance Recycling sees larger Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Appliance Recycling sees larger Q4 loss.

text.p: Appliance Recycling Centers of America Inc said it expects to report a substantially larger than planned net loss in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The larger-than-expected loss is due to write-offs and expenses tied to closings in the fourth quarter of three recycling centers and 12 Encore retail stores, it said.

"Savings in overhead and other operating expenses generated by closing these centers and Encore stores is expected to provide the opportunity for the company to return to profitability in 1997," it said.
After the closings, the company will have four recycling centers and 14 retail outlets for reconditioned appliances.

The company said it is closing its Encore stores and centers in the Washington, D.C., Hartford, Conn., and Oakland, Calif., markets, as well as its retail stores in Southern California. It will continue operating its Los Angeles appliance recycling center, it said.
The Encore reconditioned appliance business will continue to serve Minneapolis/St. Paul, St. Louis and Columbus, Ohio, the company said.

The Encore outlets and centers to close in the fourth quarter failed to meet specified growth and profit objectives, the company said, adding that it has elected to defer future expansion of its Encore retail network until after 1997.
ARCA is the nation's largest recycler of major household appliances.
